question_text: Which term of the G.P. 5, −10, 20, −40, … is 320?

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — say what r is and how the sign of the term decides your answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the nth term of the G.P.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both a = 5 and r = −2 must be written. The minus sign in r is what makes the terms alternate.
steps.memory_tip: Divide any term by the one before it: −10 ÷ 5 = −2, so the signs alternate.
lines: (r is a term divided by the term before it)
For a G.P., the nth term is  aₙ = a rⁿ⁻¹

recall.must_convey: That a = 5, r = −2 and the equation 5(−2)ⁿ⁻¹ = 320 are written.
accept: first term five and common ratio minus two
divide the second term by the first to get the ratio
set a r to the power n minus one equal to three twenty
ratio minus two, nth term formula rasta
the ratio is negative so the terms alternate in sign

steps.why: The ratio is negative, so the terms alternate in sign. With r = −2 a term is positive only when n − 1 is even, so the sign of 320 must be checked before n is accepted.
common_mistakes: Taking r = 2 and ignoring the minus signs in the sequence.
Writing aₙ = a rⁿ, which shifts every term one place.

steps.label: Solve for n and check the sign
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The power must be even for the term to be positive. (−2)⁶ = +64, so the 7th term is +320.
steps.memory_tip: 64 = 2⁶, and an even power of a negative number is positive.

recall.must_convey: That (−2)ⁿ⁻¹ = 64 = (−2)⁶ gives n = 7, and that the even power keeps the term positive.
accept: sixty four is two to the sixth so n minus one is six
the sixth power of minus two is plus sixty four
even power kabatti sign positive, n seven
three twenty is the seventh term

steps.why: Only an even power of −2 can give a positive 64, so n − 1 must be even. The check confirms the term is +320 and not −320.
common_mistakes: Answering n = 6 by solving rⁿ = 64 instead of rⁿ⁻¹ = 64.
Saying no term equals 320 because the ratio is negative.
